description: ODC (EDIT, REFACTORING and DELETION coverage for RESOURCE and SCRIPT): the lifecycle AFTER birth. This job creates neither the resource nor the script: it inherits them from job:theme-script-resource, which created them and linked the Script to the RequiredScripts of the screen WfCovBadgeScreen, and it touches what was already written. The inherited IResource changes its Description, TargetDirectory, DeployAction and Public/Shareable -- everything the type lets an author write, except what the platform maintains by itself (CreatedBy, LastModified*) and the Folder, which this module does not use -- and is then renamed; the inherited IScript changes its content (JavaScript) and properties and is also renamed. The question of the wave is the RuntimePath: it FOLLOWS, in both, because it is not stored text but a cache recomputed from TargetDirectory+Name (resource) and from Module+Name (script) -- the .js stops being served at the old URL without anyone being told, the same trap as the URLPath of an exposed REST method. Along the way the job shows a write that the PLATFORM UNDOES: with DeployAction Ignore, Resource.RefreshState stores the Path in previousPath and sets it to null, so writing TargetDirectory BEFORE the DeployAction is writing into the void; the first version of this job failed exactly like that, with 'Data property mismatch: TargetDirectory expected audit/templates, actual null' and a clean Verify. The BINARY content of the resource is the only thing left untouched, and not for lack of a verb: the Model API V1 exposes ResourceContent read-only in both lanes. At the end the inherited Script is DELETED, but only after handling whoever references it: a successor receives the consumer by replace, and only then does the delete pass without force and with brokenConsumers=0. Each change has its get before and its get after; the only new message of the job is the platform's response to the DeployAction change, declared in expectedMessages.

expectedMessages.why: It is the result of change 3, not a defect: Resource.InnerVerify only emits this message when `Referers.IsEmpty() && DeployAction == Ignore`. The inherited resource had already been born without consumers (nobody in the model points to it: it is a file delivered with the app), but it had been born with DeployAction CopyToApplicationDir, and so the base was silent. By setting Ignore, this job makes the second half of the condition true and the platform reacts. In a job that only creates, this message could not be born; and it is this, more than any get, that proves that the DeployAction write really got into the model.

ops._why: (0) THE STARTING POINT IS INHERITED: no object of this job is born here. The Script WfCovFormatting that appears in this list was created by the base job:theme-script-resource, and that is why the base is read first -- to know what exists before touching it.

(1) BEFORE, the inherited resource. Outside the job that created it there are no aliases ($resource was local to the base), so the stable reference is 'IResource:Name'. Three things to compare later: RuntimePath /InsuranceApp/templates/WfCovAuditTemplate and DisplayName templates\WfCovAuditTemplate (both derived, nobody wrote them), Public and Shareable at False, and ResourceContent at null -- the file never had bytes because the API has no way to write them (see the _why of op 10).

(2) BEFORE, who holds it: count=0, real=0. A resource is consumed by the deploy, not by the model -- and it is this zero that, further on, will pair with DeployAction Ignore to wake up the UnusedResource.

ops.value: Modelo da carta de auditoria enviada ao segurado. Description REESCRITA por resource-script-lifecycle.json: o texto anterior era o do job que criou o recurso.
ops._why: (3) CHANGE 1 - replace author text that ALREADY existed. The base had written here 'Cobertura T: recurso do modulo, entregue com a app'; this is not filling an empty field, it is overwriting what another job left.

(4) CHANGE 2 - the destination folder of the file in the published app. This write will go in and then be UNDONE by the platform in op (6): it stays here on purpose, because that is how the rule is discovered.

(5) AFTER change 2, and already half the answer to the RuntimePath question: without touching the Name, TargetDirectory says audit/templates, RuntimePath became /InsuranceApp/audit/templates/WfCovAuditTemplate and DisplayName audit\templates\WfCovAuditTemplate. Neither of the last two was written: AbstractResource.RuntimePath is a cache that CalculateRuntimePath() recomposes from TargetDirectory+Name (GetReferenceableUrl). Changing the folder already changes the URL the app serves the file at.

(6) CHANGE 3 - the property that decides whether the file is really delivered. The enum only has Ignore and CopyToApplicationDir (the four-value one is for extension modules, in another API). Two things happen after this write, and neither was asked for: the platform comments (expectedMessages) and the platform ERASES the TargetDirectory of op (4).

(7) THE WRITE THAT THE PLATFORM UNDID, read back: TargetDirectory is EMPTY and the RuntimePath shrank to /InsuranceApp/WfCovAuditTemplate -- the audit/templates of op (4) disappeared with no error, no warning and a clean Verify. The one that does this is Resource.RefreshState: when the DeployAction becomes Ignore, it stores the Path in previousPath and sets Path to null (a resource that is not delivered has no destination folder, and PropertyIsUserVisible even hides Path and RuntimePath in that state); on going back to CopyToApplicationDir, it restores previousPath. The first version of this job wrote in this order and was failed by the data contract with 'Data property mismatch: TargetDirectory expected audit/templates, actual null'. THE ORDER IS THE FIX: DeployAction first, TargetDirectory after.
(8) CHANGE 2, again, now in the right order: on top of the Ignore state. It is not a workaround for the contract -- it is the order the model requires, and op (7) is the proof of why.

(9) CHANGE 4 - the exposure of the resource, and the last author property that is missing. ONE op is enough for the TWO that the API shows: in Resource, IResource.Public returns and writes IResource.Shareable, which in turn returns and writes the Public of the model -- they are two names for the same bit, and the get (10) shows both at True after this single write. Taking effect proves that the model accepted it and that the Verify is still clean; it does not prove that the app will publish the resource to other apps.

(10) AFTER changes 1 to 4: compare with the get (1). Description, TargetDirectory, DeployAction, Public and Shareable changed, and the TargetDirectory rewritten in op (8) held even with Ignore in force, with the RuntimePath back at /InsuranceApp/audit/templates/WfCovAuditTemplate. Name, Key and ResourceContent stayed. The CONTENT of the resource is the only thing this job does not touch, and not by choice: the verb answers 'IResource X has no writable property or setter ResourceContent. Writable: CreatedBy, DeployAction, Description, Folder, LastModifiedBy, LastModifiedDate, Name, Public, Shareable, TargetDirectory', and the limit is not the kernel's -- in the Model API V1 of BOTH lanes the member is `byte[] ResourceContent { get; }` and the descriptor Resource.ResourceContentProperty is an UnderlyingModelProperty with the setter at null (BinaryPropertyDescriptor is born isReadOnly). The bytes go in through the Studio (Import Resource), not through a job.

ops.name: WfCovAuditLetter
ops._why: (11) REFACTORING of the inherited resource: the name was wrong, it is not any old template, it is the audit letter. It returns consumers=0, consistent with the usages (2).

(12) THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION, first half: the RuntimePath FOLLOWED the rename -- /InsuranceApp/audit/templates/WfCovAuditLetter -- and so did the DisplayName. There is no text propagation here at all: the cache was recomputed from the new Name. The practical consequence is that of the URLPath of an exposed REST method: whoever had this URL written by hand outside the module (a page, a CSS, an external consumer) now gets a 404 and nobody is told.

(13) AFTER: still count=0, real=0. Renaming neither creates nor loses consumers; and it is the zero of this usages, together with the Ignore of op (6), that exactly satisfies the condition of the UnusedResource.

(14) BEFORE, the inherited script: the JavaScript that the base wrote, RuntimePath /InsuranceApp/scripts/InsuranceApp.WfCovFormatting.js -- note that the NAME of the script is inside the name of the served file -- and Referrers=0. That Referrers is a trap: it is the reading of the Model API (IModelObject.Referrers), which filters out the referers with no V1 representation, and the ScriptDependency of the screen is one of them. The usages that follows counts the same object and gives 1.

(15) BEFORE, the truth about who holds it: count=1, real=1, one ScriptDependency in IMobileFlow:WfCovThemeFlow/IMobileScreen:WfCovBadgeScreen -- the RequiredScripts that the base linked. It is this consumer, invisible in the Referrers of the get (14), that later makes the delete be refused until it is handled.

(16) CHANGE 5 - the CONTENT of the script, which here really exists as a writable property (IScript.JavaScript { get; set; }), unlike ResourceContent. The inherited text had only the badge on one line; this one has two functions and real line breaks. The data contract checks this at the end: the line breaks settle as written (LF, no normalization), so the value read back is byte for byte what the job wrote.

ops.value: Helpers de formatacao do lado do cliente. Description REESCRITA por resource-script-lifecycle.json, por cima da que o job de nascimento deixou.
ops._why: (17) CHANGE 6 - another replacement of inherited author text, not an empty field.
(18) CHANGE 7 - the exposure of the inherited script, with the same design as the resource: IScript.Public and IScript.Shareable delegate to each other over the Public of the model.

(19) AFTER changes 5 to 7: compare with the get (14). JavaScript, Description and Public changed -- and Shareable became True with no op, which is the living proof of the delegation explained in (18). The RuntimePath did NOT change, because nobody has touched the Name yet: the cache depends on the name, not on the content. HasSyntaxErrors is still False, that is, the platform re-read the new JavaScript.

ops.name: WfCovBadgeFormatting
ops._why: (20) REFACTORING of the inherited script, WITH the real consumer linked. expressionsRewritten=0 is honest: no expression reads this script, what holds it is a ScriptDependency.

(21) THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION, second half: RuntimePath became /InsuranceApp/scripts/InsuranceApp.WfCovBadgeFormatting.js. The .js file that the browser fetches CHANGED URL just because the script was renamed, with no op on the RuntimePath and no warning at all.

(22) AFTER the rename: the same ScriptDependency, with the SAME key as in the usages (15). The screen followed the object, not the name or the URL -- and that is why the module stays valid after a rename that breaks hand-written URLs.

ops.name: WfCovBadgeHelpers
ops._why: (23) HANDLE WHO REFERENCES, step 1: the successor. It is the only thing this job creates, and that is why it carries the Wf prefix. The screen still needs a script; deleting the inherited one without giving it a replacement would be breaking the screen, not maintaining it.

ops.value: Versao mantida dos helpers de badge. Substituiu o WfCovFormatting herdado.

ops._why: (24) The freshly created successor: own Key, RuntimePath /InsuranceApp/scripts/InsuranceApp.WfCovBadgeHelpers.js and nobody pointing to it yet -- here the Referrers=0 of the get is true, unlike (14), because there is no ScriptDependency for it to hide. The alias $sucessor exists only because THIS job created it -- it is the difference between what is inherited and what is added.

(25) HANDLE WHO REFERENCES, step 2: repoint. It is not search and replace of text, it is the ReplaceReferences that the Studio itself uses; the method runs on each CONSUMER. It returns rewired=1 with touched naming the ScriptDependency of the screen, stillPointingAtFrom=0 and consumersOfTo=1. The ScriptDependency keeps the same key: the target changed, not the consumer.
(26) The inherited one has to be at zero before the delete.
(27) And the inherited consumer is now here, with the usual key.

(28) DELETION, and only now: brokenConsumers=0 and no force. Without ops (23)-(25) this same delete is refused -- 'delete: refused, IScript WfCovFormatting is used by 1 consumer(s): IMobileFlow:WfCovThemeFlow/IMobileScreen:WfCovBadgeScreen/ScriptDependency' -- because the refusal reads the native referers, the same ones that the Referrers=0 of the get (14) was hiding. The data contract does not charge for the writes of ops (16)-(18): what the job itself deleted on purpose is fulfilled proof, not lost proof.

ops.name: WfCovFormatting
ops._why: (29) It is only now that this name is free: before the delete the rename would be refused for a collision in the same scope.

(30) THE THIRD LESSON ABOUT THE RUNTIMEPATH: it went back to /InsuranceApp/scripts/InsuranceApp.WfCovFormatting.js, the exact URL of the deleted script -- but the Key is the successor's, not the original's. Since it is derived from the name, the RuntimePath FOLLOWS the object but does not IDENTIFY it: another object with the same name inherits the same URL. The Description still cites 'WfCovFormatting herdado', a name that is now its own, because Description is author text and no rename touches it.

ops.name: WfCovBadgeFormatting
ops._why: (31) Empty list: the inherited script really left the module.

(32) THE FINAL STATE OF WHO REFERENCED IT: the inherited screen still requires a script and nothing in it needed to be rewritten by hand. It was the target of the dependency that changed, twice (rename and replace), always underneath the same consumer.

(33) WHAT STAYED: the renamed resource, with the four author writes of this job (five properties changed, because Public and Shareable are the same bit) and the RuntimePath derived from the two fields that this job touched. The module closes valid, with a single new message -- the one that the DeployAction change provoked.
